title: Measurement of antimicrobial activity under reducing conditions in a modified radial diffusion assay
protocol: Dissolve 15 g of TSB powder in 500 ml ddH₂O.
Autoclave the solution to prepare 1x Tryptic Soy Broth (TSB).
Prepare 200 mM monobasic phosphate buffer by dissolving 13.8 g of NaH₂PO₄ in 500 ml ddH₂O.
Prepare 200 mM dibasic phosphate buffer by dissolving 17.8 g of Na₂HPO₄ in 500 ml ddH₂O.
Mix 47.5 ml of monobasic NaP with 202.5 ml dibasic NaP.
Add 250 ml H₂O to the mixture.
Autoclave the mixed buffer solution.
Dilute 100 mM Phosphate Buffer 1:10 with H₂O, making a final volume of 100 ml.
Autoclave the diluted phosphate buffer.
Add 0.5 g EEO-agarose into a 100 ml bottle for low nutrition gel preparation.
Add 0.5 ml 1x TSB to the mixture for low nutrition gel.
Add 5 ml of Phosphate Buffer 100 mM, pH 7.4 to the mixture for low nutrition gel.
Adjust the final volume to 50 ml with ddH₂O for low nutrition gel.
Adjust the pH to 7.4 with diluted HCl (1:100 or 1:10) for low nutrition gel.
Autoclave the mixture in a 100 ml bottle at 121°C for 20 min for low nutrition gel.
Store the prepared low nutrition gel at room temperature for short term.
Add 0.5 g EEO-agarose into a 100 ml bottle.
Add 3 g TSB powder to the mixture.
Add 5 ml of phosphate buffer (100 mM, pH 7.4) to the mixture.
Add ddH₂O to reach a final volume of 50 ml.
Autoclave the solution in a 100 ml bottle for 20 min at 121°C.
Store the autoclaved solution at room temperature for short-term use.
Prepare anaerobic bacteria from kryo-culture.
Incubate the bacteria on Columbia Blood-Agar plates in an anaerobic jar for about 48 hours.
Transfer the bacteria into a 50 ml falcon containing 10 ml of 1x TSB.
Place the falcon without lid into an anaerobic jar and incubate at 37°C for about 16 hours without shaking.
Pre-chill centrifuge at 4°C.
Place sterile phosphate buffer (10 mM, pH 7.4) on ice.
Melt underlay gel in microwave.
Transfer the melted gel to 50 ml falcons with 10-ml aliquots each.
Maintain the gel liquid by placing it in a 46°C water bath.
Add 5-20 µl DTT into liquid gel from the 1 M stock solution.
Centrifuge bacterial overnight culture in Falcons for 10 minutes at 4°C and 900 x g.
Wash bacterial sediment with 10 ml ice-cold sterile phosphate buffer, pH 7.4.
Centrifuge bacterial culture for 10 minutes at 4°C and 900 x g.
Resuspend sediment in 5 ml ice-cold sterile phosphate buffer, pH 7.4.
Determine optical density at 620 nm against a buffer control (10 mM phosphate buffer).
Add 10-20 µl resazurine into liquid gel to achieve a final concentration of 1–2 µg/ml.
Adjust bacterial culture to OD<sub>620nm</sub> = 0.1.
Use 150 – 300 µl of bacterial culture for the assay.
Add bacterial suspension into 10 ml of warm underlay gel and mix gently.
Pour the gel containing bacteria into square-petri-dishes placed on an even surface.
Let the gel solidify for about 30 minutes at room temperature.
Punch 6 x 6 wells into the gel.
Discard gel pieces using a sterile pipette tip or Pasteur pipette connected to a vacuum pump.
Fill up to 5 µl of proteins, dissolved in H₂O or 0.01% acetic acid, into the wells.
Include negative control (H₂O or 0.01% acetic acid) and positive control (for example lysozyme, depending on bacteria tested).
Let protein solutions diffuse into the gel (short storage at 37°C or room temperature).
Place plates into anaerobic jar for 3 hours.
Melt overlay gel in microwave.
Transfer melted overlay gel to 50 ml falcons, 10 ml each.
Maintain overlay gel at 46°C.
Add DTT and resazurine according to the corresponding underlay gel.
Pour 10 ml of nutrient-rich overlay gel onto each underlay gel.
Let overlay gel solidify.
Place plate upside-down in anaerobic incubator until bacterial lawn is clearly visible (16 to 48 hours).
